cases.query: Under UN Regulation No. 94, what is the maximum permitted Thorax Compression Criterion (ThCC) for the 50th percentile male dummy in frontal impact, and in which clause is it specified?
cases.answer:
The maximum permitted Thorax Compression Criterion (ThCC) is 42 mm [S1]. 
It is specified in UN R94 §5.2.1.4 [S1].
cases.ground_truth: UN R94 limits ThCC (thorax compression criterion) to 42 mm for the 50th percentile male dummy in frontal impact. The limit is specified in clause 5.2.1.4 of the injury criteria provisions.

cases.query: How does UN Regulation No. 129 define an i-Size child restraint system and what sizing principle does it use?
cases.answer:
UN Regulation No. 129 defines an i-Size child restraint system as an Enhanced Child Restraint System that is designed for use in i-Size seating positions [S1]. 
The Regulation uses a stature range principle for sizing, with the label on the Enhanced Child Restraint System informing the user of the appropriate method of restraint of the child over the entire stature range declared by the manufacturer [S3]. 
The size range for which the Enhanced Child Restraint System has been designed is indicated on the approval mark [S4]. 
The i-Size category is primarily designed for use in i-Size seating positions, when the Enhanced Child Restraint Systems are fitted in conformity with the vehicle manufacturer's instructions [S4].
cases.ground_truth: UN R129 defines enhanced child restraint systems under the i-Size approach using height-based classification rather than mass-based groups. i-Size systems are integrated child restraint systems designed for defined height classes with ISOFIX-based installation and enhanced protection requirements.

cases.query: Under UN Regulation No. 16, what are the emergency locking retractor (ELR) requirements in paragraph 6.2.5.3.1? Answer with an explicit section citation.
cases.answer:
The emergency locking retractor (ELR) requirements in paragraph 6.2.5.3.1 of UN Regulation No. 16 are specified in §7.6.2, which states that the locking must have occurred when the deceleration of the vehicle reaches 0.45 g in the case of type 4 or 0.85 g in the case of type 4N retractors [S1].
* The locking threshold for type 4 retractors is 0.45 g [S1].
* The locking threshold for type 4N retractors is 0.85 g [S1].
The requirements for the emergency locking retractor are further detailed in paragraph 6.2.5.3.1.1, 6.2.5.3.1.2, and 6.2.5.3.1.3 of §7.6.2 [S1].
cases.ground_truth: UN R16 paragraph 6.2.5.3.1 sets requirements for emergency locking retractors, including locking performance under vehicle deceleration and belt payout conditions relevant to occupant restraint. The response must cite §6.2.5.3.1 explicitly and ground statements in retrieved UN R16 text.

cases.query: How does UN Regulation No. 16 define a "safety-belt reminder" (SBR) system and in which clause is it defined?
cases.answer:
UN Regulation No. 16 defines a "safety-belt reminder" (SBR) system as a system constituted by a detection of an unfastened safety-belt and by two levels of driver's alert: a first level warning and a second level warning [S2]. 
The definition of the "safety-belt reminder" system is found in §2.40 of UN Regulation No. 16 [S2].
cases.ground_truth: UN R16 clause 2.40 defines the safety-belt reminder as a system that alerts the driver when he/she does not use the safety-belt, constituted by detection of an unfastened safety-belt and two levels of driver alert (a first-level warning and a second, stronger alert).
